title: Length of Longest Fibonacci Subsequence
summary: An array arr is considered Fibonacci-like if it contains at least three elements where each element (except the last two) is the sum of the preceding two.
statement: An array arr is considered Fibonacci-like if it contains at least three elements where each element (except the last two) is the sum of the preceding two. Given a strictly increasing array of positive integers, find the length of the longest subsequence that follows this Fibonacci-like pattern. If no such subsequence exists, return 0. A subsequence is formed by removing zero or more elements from the original array while maintaining the order of the remaining elements.
constraints: arr is strictly increasing with at most 1,000 elements.
Return longest Fibonacci-like subsequence length, or zero if none has length three.
hints: A Fibonacci-like subsequence is determined by its last two values.
Use pair DP and a value-to-index lookup for the required predecessor.
For pair j,k find i with arr[i]=arr[k]-arr[j]; dp[j,k]=dp[i,j]+1.
Strict increase makes the predecessor unique and i<j enforces subsequence order.
editorial: Strict increase makes the predecessor unique and i<j enforces subsequence order.

tests.explanation: One longest subsequence is 1,2,3,5,8 of length five.
